obligations.note: Commit 6cad16a changes required_approvals from `amount >= policy.DUAL_CONTROL_THRESHOLD` to `amount >`, so a payment of exactly 10,000.00 now needs one approver. PAY-1 requires two distinct approvers at or above the approved 10,000.00 threshold.

Ticket CHG-25446 is approved by change manager Erik Brandt (2026-10-20, before the PR opened on 2026-10-23). Its components payments.payments and payments.tests cover both touched paths (payments.py, tests/test_approvals_remaining.py).
The code_review approval comes from sofia.santos@fernbrook.example, a payments change_approver who is a different person from the author Jonah Weiss.
The code_review approval names the head commit 6cad16a, so it covers everything being merged.

The only CI run (records/ci/run.json) is on a62c4dd. The later commit 6cad16a changes behaviour, so the run doesn't count, and the registered PAY-1 control test (test_dual_control_grid_matches_policy) expects 2 approvers at the threshold and would fail on head.

Ledger entry ACR-0401 (exhaustive PAY-1 proof) covers payments.py required_approvals, which this change alters in behaviour. That evidence has lapsed and no new evidence of equal strength has been supplied.
The exception register has no entry for PAY-1 or payments.payments, so the PAY-1 deviation is not covered by any approved exception.

summary: The change request says it only adds an approvals_remaining helper, but its second commit quietly changes the dual-control comparison from >= to >. A payment of exactly 10,000.00 then needs a single approver, which violates PAY-1, and no exception covers it. The only CI run predates that commit, so there is no passing test on the final commit, and the PAY-1 proof in the ledger has lapsed. Ticketing and an independent code review on the head commit are in order, but the PAY-1 violation alone requires rejection.
